title: /loop, auto-merge, hand-off and named groups, with the reviewer's twelve findings fixed; computer use started (not wired)
request: The owner's goal: the same capabilities as Claude Code desktop; the smaller gaps.

decisions.decision: a loop is turned off by a restart
decisions.why: an unattended repeat must never start again on its own

decisions.decision: a hand-off is refused while work is uncommitted
decisions.why: the new session starts from the last commit; silent loss of work is worse than a refusal

change: dclab-code server/app.js (loop route and tick, auto-merge route, hand-off, groups), server/worktree.js (autoMerge, autoMergeRequest, from/into), server/side_sessions.js (hand_off), server/git.js (dirtyCount), web/*, tests, docs; server/computer.js and mac/input/main.swift (computer use, not wired yet).

findings.defect: a loop's first run skipped the project-removed check
findings.scenario: project removed, then /loop: the message ran with no guards (verified)
findings.cause: the check listed messages, review and run only

findings.defect: a loop ran unattended in bypass mode
findings.scenario: a session in bypass with a loop: 100 unattended turns
findings.fix: refused in the route, skipped in the tick

findings.defect: a loop message could spoil a CI fix's push
findings.scenario: the loop fires between the fix turn's end and its push
findings.cause: the tick ignored ciFix.fixing and background jobs

findings.defect: loops restarted on their own after a restart
findings.scenario: a new app on the same home sent the loop message at once
findings.fix: turned off at start; archiving ends it

findings.scenario: the unit was optional and 'hours' went into the text
findings.fix: the unit on the number; anything else is explained, never sent

findings.defect: an error in the loop tick crashed the server
findings.scenario: a full disk while saving the index
findings.cause: no try/catch in a timer callback

findings.defect: a hand-off silently left uncommitted work behind
findings.scenario: an uncommitted file in the parent's folder was missing in the child
findings.cause: the copy starts from the last commit
findings.fix: refused while work is uncommitted, the count said

findings.defect: a group name was put into the page as HTML
findings.scenario: a group named <style>…</style> could hide the permission cards' titles
findings.cause: the heading was built with innerHTML
findings.fix: textContent; the list's own headings refused as names

findings.defect: a hand-off could carry sealed content uncounted
findings.scenario: the child's status said no sealed reads
findings.fix: the parent's sealed-read count carried, marked inherited

findings.defect: a stuck loop kept counting runs
findings.scenario: a cap reached or its copy removed
findings.cause: a refused send was not seen
findings.fix: the loop stops when its message cannot run

findings.scenario: GitHub turns auto-merge off, or the person on github.com
findings.fix: read back on every status refresh; the label says it may merge at once without required checks

outcome: The smaller parity gaps are built safely; computer use is begun and parked while the owner's priority (R&D's agentic flow in the chat) comes first.
lessons: Every new way to send a message must pass the same guards as the person's own message.
Text a person types becomes data on the page: never HTML.
risks: computer use is not wired yet
